clue.text: Hilton's high-spot Gran hails excitedly

indicators.note: doing something excitedly suggests agitation, so the letters of the two words are stirred up

explanation.surface: An elderly woman greets someone with great enthusiasm at the top of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hilton' looks like the hotel chain, but it is James Hilton, the novelist who invented this Himalayan paradise in Lost Horizon. 'excitedly' rearranges GRAN HAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon places this idyllic hidden valley high in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Plucky player

parts.note: reads as a brave sportsperson, but means a musician who plucks strings

explanation.definitionFit: A musician on the harp plucks its strings, so is literally a plucky player.

clue.text: Ne plus ultra parts perhaps, non-aligned

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: parts in the sense of separates and redistributes, so the letters are broken up and put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Latin tag about the highest point gets split up, as if from a neutral observer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plus' joins NE and ULTRA, and 'parts perhaps' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A country not aligned with any bloc is described as neutral in a conflict.

clue.text: Ratty, for example, running between banks?

explanation.definitionFit: Ratty, the water rat in The Wind in the Willows, lives by a river; the word also describes anything along riverbanks, where water runs between banks.

clue.text: Jack transported away

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
transported means carried or dispatched, that is sent

explanation.surface: A sailor has been shipped off somewhere distant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone away is not present, the adjective's ordinary sense.

clue.text: Old Bob, we hear, clutching cent that is accepted in Austria

indicators.note: one word clutching another holds it inside, so the coin's name wraps the letter for cent

parts.note: a bob was British slang for the old shilling coin

explanation.surface: A former British coin, which sounds similar, holds a cent and is legal tender in Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' adds that the result sounds just like the British coin. A bob was the old British shilling, worth twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The schilling was Austria's currency before the euro, so it was the money accepted there.

clue.text: Frolic between US spies is a bloomer

indicators.note: one piece sits between the letters of another, so the spies' initials go round the frolic

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a lark is a bit of fun or frolic

explanation.surface: Playful mischief among American agents turns out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' looks like a mistake, but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarkia is a flowering garden plant, so it is a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Narcissist has come again, sadly

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are in a sorry, disordered state and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone self-absorbed has returned, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges COME AGAIN; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcissist is vain and self-obsessed, exactly what an egomaniac is.

clue.text: Encourage the record of accumulation of work

parts.note: to back someone is to support or encourage them
a log is a written record, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Support a written account of how much work has piled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Work piled up undone is a backlog, an accumulation of tasks.

clue.text: Crow hit?

explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to exult over a victory; a hit is a great success or win.

clue.text: Witty remark of retired soldier in record hit

indicators.note: one piece goes in the middle of the others, so the turned soldier sits inside the record and hit

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
to ram is to hit forcefully

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the soldier's letters are written backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran's clever saying is captured on a hit recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the soldier backwards before 'in' places him inside the record and hit; 'of' is a link. A GI is an American serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, pointed saying, a quip.

clue.text: One who turns up the volume at work

definitions.text: One who turns up the volume at work

parts.words: One who turns up the volume at work
parts.note: reads as someone raising the sound, but a volume is a book, which this worker finds for readers

explanation.definitionFit: A person in charge of a book collection retrieves volumes for borrowers.

clue.text: Attribute of an old writer

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
a scribe copied manuscripts by hand in earlier times

explanation.surface: A quality belonging to a medieval copyist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attribute' looks like a noun (a quality) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to a source is to credit it to them, the verb sense.

clue.text: Entire hedge, in front of No 10,new?

indicators.note: in front of means the delaying word comes before the rest

parts.note: to hedge is to stall or avoid committing
the number ten written as digits looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Is the whole of the evasion outside Downing Street something fresh?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entire' as a noun is an ungelded male horse. No 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: An entire is a horse that has not been castrated, a breeding male.

clue.text: Girl all set to come out

indicators.note: coming out suggests a fresh arrangement emerging, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman is fully prepared for her debut in society.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Wherein hot-rod drivers, were once busy?

definitions.text: Wherein hot-rod drivers, were once busy?

parts.words: Wherein hot-rod drivers, were once busy?
parts.note: suggests fast-car enthusiasts, but describes workers hammering red-hot rivets into vessels being built

explanation.definitionFit: Riveters drove heated rods into hulls in the docks where vessels were built.

clue.text: When union offers are made from the other side?

definitions.text: When union offers are made from the other side?

parts.words: When union offers are made from the other side?
parts.note: suggests trade-union negotiations, but refers to the tradition that women may propose marriage on 29 February

explanation.definitionFit: By tradition a woman may propose marriage in a year with an extra day in February.

clue.text: Get people on-line in transparent rainwear

indicators.note: in signals the letters are tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Persuade folk to wear see-through waterproofs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on-line' means onto a railway line, not the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a train, putting passengers on the railway.

clue.text: I am taking public service vehicles, with these feet

parts.note: taken as written
buses provide public transport

explanation.surface: Someone says they will travel by bus, walking only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' are metrical feet in verse, not limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An iambus is a metrical foot of a short then long syllable, so the plural names such feet.

clue.text: Composer from USSR sat uncomfortably

indicators.note: sitting uncomfortably suggests shifting position, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Soviet composer squirmed in his seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann and Richard Strauss were famous composers.

clue.text: Find part of the saga Michael wrote is asexual

indicators.note: part of says the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Locate a section of a long tale Michael penned that lacks romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamic describes reproduction without sexual union, a biological term.

clue.text: Not getting on, decline what is inferior

parts.note: to age is to decline with the years
less means smaller or lower in rank

explanation.surface: Refusing the lesser option keeps one from growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' means growing old here, not progressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless means not growing old, timeless.

clue.text: Fashionable church feature to hearten people

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a spire is the pointed tower on a church

explanation.surface: A trendy steeple lifts the spirits of the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire people is to encourage and uplift them.

clue.text: Build business that is dishonestly prearranged

parts.note: to put up a structure is to build it
a job is a piece of work or business

explanation.surface: Construct an enterprise rigged in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigged scheme planned in secret, often an inside crime, is called this.

clue.text: Dutch house with no cooking equipment

parts.note: O stands for nought, nothing
a range is a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: A Netherlands home lacking a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' means a royal dynasty: the Dutch royal family is the House of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch royal dynasty is the House of Orange-Nassau.

clue.text: Rector set bread out for robin

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman leaves crumbs for a garden bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the two words as written to give EDBREAST; the robin is called this in Britain from its orange-red chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is named for its red chest.

clue.text: A limping American lawyer in a Spanish tree-lined walk

parts.note: lame means unable to walk properly
a DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A hobbling US attorney strolls a Spanish avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a public promenade shaded by trees, in Spanish-speaking places.

clue.text: Hermit taking salt, as starter, in vinegar acid

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the acid's name takes in the letter

parts.note: acetic acid is the acid in vinegar

indicators.note: as starter means only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A recluse adds salt as an appetizer to sour vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives a life of austere self-denial, as an ascetic does.

clue.text: Handy thing to brighten up old crocks

definitions.text: Handy thing to brighten up old crocks

parts.words: Handy thing to brighten up old crocks
parts.note: suggests restoring decrepit cars, but crocks are earthenware pots and plates cleaned by a cloth in the hand

explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for washing up cleans plates and pots, crockery.

clue.text: English comfortable to check interacting biological communities

parts.note: cosy means snug, comfortable
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: The English are relaxed about holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecologists study communities of organisms interacting with their environment as such systems.
